name: MathlibAnnex.PluckerBody.isCompact_generators
title: Compactness of the signed generator set

content.display_title: Compactness of the signed generator set
content.one_sentence_role: Passes compactness from contractions to their two signed minor images.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $n,N\in\mathbb N_0$ and give $E=\mathbb R^n$ and $F=\mathbb R^N$ their coordinate sup norms. Let $\lambda_n$ be the fixed coordinate Lebesgue measure on $E$. Let $p:E\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous real seminorm with specified constants $a_p,b_p>0$ such that
$$a_p\|x\|_\infty\le p(x)\le b_p\|x\|_\infty\qquad(x\in E).$$

The lower bound makes $p$ a norm. Its closed unit ball and real reference volume are
$$K_p=\{x:p(x)\le1\},\qquad v_p=\lambda_n(K_p)\in(0,\infty).$$
Here and below a finite Lebesgue measure is read as a real number when used as a scalar.

Let $\mathcal I_{n,N}$ be the finite set of increasing $n$-tuples of distinct rows from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. The minor-coordinate space $\mathbb R^{\mathcal I_{n,N}}$ carries its sup norm. For a linear map $B:E\to F$, put $B_{ij}=(Be_j)_i$ in the standard coordinate basis. Write $\Pi_n(B)$ for its maximal-minor vector and $\mathcal V_p(B)$ for that vector scaled by $v_p$. Their coordinates and scaling are
$$\Pi_n(B)_I=\det(B_{i_a,j})_{a,j=1}^n,\qquad\mathcal V_p(B)=v_p\Pi_n(B)\quad(I=(i_1<\cdots<i_n)).$$

A $p$-contraction is a linear map $B:E\to F$ satisfying $\|Bz\|_\infty\le p(z)$ for every $z\in E$. Let $\mathcal C_p^N$ be their set, and put
$$\mathcal G_p^N=\{\mathcal V_p(B),-\mathcal V_p(B):B\in\mathcal C_p^N\}.$$

Then $\mathcal G_p^N$ is compact.
content.assumptions: The source and target are finite real coordinate spaces with sup norms. The seminorm $p$ is continuous and has the stated positive lower and upper comparison constants. The measure is the original coordinate Lebesgue measure. The dimensions $n,N$ may be zero. When $n=0$, the unique empty minor has determinant $1$; when $N<n$, the minor-index set is empty and its function space has one element. Neither case is excluded.
content.conclusion: Compactness holds in the usual topology of the finite-coordinate space $\mathbb R^{\mathcal I_{n,N}}$.
content.proof_summary: Bound the operators and then take their continuous signed images.

proof_steps.text:
**Make the contraction set compact.** Give the finite-dimensional operator space $\mathcal L(E,F)$ its induced operator norm
$$\|B\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\sup_{\|x\|_\infty\le1}\|Bx\|_\infty.$$
Then
$$\mathcal C_p^N=\bigcap_{x\in E}\{B:\|Bx\|_\infty\le p(x)\},\qquad\|B\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le b_p\quad(B\in\mathcal C_p^N).$$
For fixed $x$, evaluation $B\mapsto Bx$ is continuous, so every set in the intersection is closed. The norm bound follows from $\|Bx\|_\infty\le p(x)\le b_p\|x\|_\infty$. Thus the contraction set is closed and contained in the closed operator ball of radius $b_p$. Finite dimensionality makes it compact.

**Take two continuous images.** Put $Q=\mathcal V_p(\mathcal C_p^N)$. Then
$$\mathcal G_p^N=Q\cup(-Q).$$
This is [the image-union identity](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Convex/PluckerBody.lean#L52-L64). Matrix entries are continuous in the operator, determinants are finite polynomials, and the scalar $v_p$ is fixed. These are [continuity of maximal minors](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/MaximalMinor.lean#L179-L192) and [continuity after volume scaling](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/VolumeScaledMaximalMinor.lean#L48-L55). The continuous-image theorem applied first to $\mathcal C_p^N$ and then to negation on $Q$ makes $Q$ and $-Q$ compact. Substitution into the displayed union gives compactness of $\mathcal G_p^N$.
